request: Build a small Jac web app with a job queue that streams progress. Jobs are added to a queue and run by a handler that reports progress from 0 to 100. Every state change (waiting, active, progress, completed, failed) is published as an event and the page shows a live progress bar per job. A failing job is retried up to a configured number of attempts.
acceptance: Progress may not go down or above 100: reporting 50 then 30 is rejected.
A job whose handler fails twice with attempts=3 and then succeeds ends completed with 3 attempts made.
Listeners receive a job's events in order: waiting, active, progress updates, then completed or failed.
constraints: Use Jac 0.36.1 and a fullstack Jac app.
Deliver events through an in-process event bus that tests can subscribe to; no sockets, no network, no background servers.
Keep the logic deterministic: time is passed in, never read from the clock inside the rules.

source.note: Requirements written in English from the project's feature description; no code or text copied. Only one feature slice is reproduced.
